workflow: ImageGen component library -> chroma-key alpha extraction -> deterministic toroidal assembly -> taste approval -> MM

generation.prompt: Create exactly sixteen separate individual hand-cut blue-grey slate roofing tile sprites in a clean 4-column by 4-row component sheet, matching the supplied large slate-roof sprites' grounded pixel art, restrained dither, and subtle within-family color variation. Every tile must be upright in the same orientation: straight or squared attachment edge at the top and visibly rounder, scalloped, or softly irregular exposed edge at the bottom. No tile may be upside down, sideways, rotated, mirrored, diamond-shaped, or pointed upward. Use a perfectly flat solid #00ff00 chroma-key background with no shadows, gradients, texture, grid lines, or cell borders. Keep one isolated slate centered in each implied cell at equal approximate scale with generous separation. Use a coherent dark blue-grey family with narrow natural variation across cool charcoal, smoky blue-grey, muted steel-blue, and a few slightly lighter weathered pieces; avoid a harsh checkerboard. Use broad quiet slate planes, slight handmade silhouette variation, and sparse mineral texture. Exactly 16 slates; neutral local albedo; no cast shadow, ambient occlusion, bevel lighting, vignette, labels, text, watermark, mortar, roof field, cracks, moss, damage story, or extra objects.

alpha.validation: RGBA; 1254x1254; all four corners alpha 0; opaque coverage 0.4928

rules: components are never rotated or flipped
rounded exposed edges remain visibly downward
identical variants may not touch horizontally or vertically
the variant grid and geometry close on both repeat axes
